Qur’an & Arabic
Learning Centre

A working plan for an after-school program for children ages 5–12. The kickoff team must confirm family interest, costs and safe staffing before setting an opening date.

Download kickoff deck ↓

Parent research

Capture consented, anonymous feedback about family needs, schedule fit, Hifz and Arabic goals, and concerns. Interview notes stay in the interviewer’s browser and are not submitted to a server.

Open parent interview form →

The proposed school day

2 batches3:00–5:00 pm and 5:10–7:10 pm. Each child attends one fixed batch five days a week.
40 seatsMaximum planned capacity across both batches. Family demand still needs to be measured.
120 minutes80 minutes for Hifz, 30 for Arabic and a 10-minute break.

Placement and progress

Teachers assess Qur’an and Arabic skills separately. Children may focus on reading foundations, Tajweed, new memorization or retention. Families can try one session before reserving a seat. The plan calls for weekly updates and a fuller monthly report.

Before opening

01　Confirm demand and fees

Ask families which batch they could attend and what monthly fee they could sustain. Compare likely paid seats with staffing and facility costs.

02　Confirm teaching coverage

Each full batch of 20 requires two Hifz teachers and a dedicated Arabic teacher. Assign responsibility for placement, trial sessions and family updates.

03　Set safeguarding procedures

Name a safeguarding lead and document attendance, supervision and authorized pickup before enrollment begins.
